native_result.query: How does the effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP compare between developing countries and countries in Sub-Saharan Africa?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP is more pronounced in developing countries outside of Sub-Saharan Africa compared to those within it
native_result.HypoB: **Natural-language hypothesis (data-grounded, associational).** In the supplied World Bank panel the relationship between the education-expenditure share (series NY.ADJ.AEDU.GN.ZS, "Adjusted savings: education expenditure, % of GNI") and per-capita GDP (only per-capita income series present is GNI per capita, constant 2015 US$) is *negative* in both groups but not statistically distinguishable between them: in the headline pooled panel for 1991-2015 with primary-enrollment, secondary-enrollment, exports-growth and labor-force controls (N=30, N_SSA=5, N_LMC=25; HC1 + Newey-West HAC standard errors), the LMC slope is −0.189 (p=0.15), the SSA slope is −0.181, and the SSA-vs-LMC interaction (β3, the comparison) is +0.008 with p≈0.96 under both HC1 and HAC(lag=4) SE — i.e. no detectable difference. The same null holds in the full 1975-2015 specification (β3=+0.012, p=0.93) and with a linear time trend (β3=+0.139, p=0.33). The single window in which the interaction is statistically significant is 2011-2015 (β3=+0.49, p=0.0002), but SSA GNI per capita is observed only for 2011-2015 (N_SSA=5) in this dataset, so that model is identified on 5 SSA outcome points and should not be treated as evidence. The simple within-group OLS slopes of log(GNI p.c.) on edu-exp share are also negative in both groups (LMC −0.45 to −0.91 across windows; SSA ≈ −0.10), a pattern at least partly mechanical because the regressor is a ratio with GNI itself in its denominator. We deliberately make no causal claim: endogeneity, reverse causation (higher GNI→more savings capacity), omitted institutional/conflict variables, and autocorrelation in panel residuals all bias these estimates in ways the data cannot resolve.
